title: Machine Learning by Kate Vozella at Manhattan Neighborhood Network #m...
transcript: This play about a social experiment left me just as disoriented as the subjects. Staged in a venue that feels aptly sterile, Machine Learning depicts a research study on human intimacy in order to train “companions.” The two couples, both on the rocks, pass the unspecified amount of time by drinking, bickering, and rehashing some backstories that explain their relationship issues. I was initially excited to learn more about this research project, but it never ended up being the true focus of the play. I see now that the primary intent is just to illustrate human relationships, but the vagueness in the premise is distracting — I had too many questions, and I kept looking for clues to help me answer them. When I wasn't wondering if we'd get more context, I was entertained by a super unhinged character played by Delaney Rowe. She's the resident pot stirrer and master of psychological manipulation, rage baiting everyone else for the hell of it. I know the play is about human research for new technology, but I feel like she's the machine, socially engineering the other participants any way that she can. I'm honestly not sure if I've identified a dual meaning behind the title or if I'm just grasping at straws at this point, trying to make sense of a piece that has a cool premise, but ultimately lacks clarity.
